text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyHow Our Eyes Betray Us When We LieSubtle shifts in gaze can signal we’re hiding somethingJCBy Jake Currie2:00 PM CST on November 19, 2026Add Nautilus to Google“It takes two to lie: one to lie and one to listen,” isn’t just a famous quote from Homer Simpson, it’s also the spirit of an actual experiment from a new study published in PLOS One. Psychologists from Ulm University in Germany recently investigated how our eyes react when we’re trying to deceive another actual person.   Powered By 10 ShareNextStayHere’s how they arranged the experiment: We’ll call our protagonist “Participant” and their partner “Mentalist” (because that’s what they called them in the study. During the investigation this pair sat facing one another at a table. Participant first selected a card with a number from one to six (if it’s important to your mental image, they resembled Uno cards). A screen visible to both Participant and Mentalist then showed the cards in sequence for five seconds each. Afterwards, Mentalist got to ask Participant some yes or no questions (i.e., “Is your card even?”) to try to determine which card they picked.Read more: “The Galaxies in Your Eyes”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
